scoring_justification: Paper-reported values (Mn content, Ms temperatures, driving forces) are used as reference gold; recomputing from raw artifacts without the proprietary Thermo-Calc database environment is not feasible, but the agent's computed numbers are compared to paper-derived references with generous tolerances that absorb toolchain spread.

hidden_assets.purpose: Inline gold tables for Mn content vs temperature, equilibrium Ms vs temperature, paraequilibrium driving forces vs temperature, and paraequilibrium austenite Ms
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from paper Fig 3, Fig 2, Fig 4, and the text statement Ms=-10°C.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Manual digitization of paper figures and direct extraction of the reported value -10°C; consistent with reference solve.sh which writes these exact values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: All numbers are taken from the source paper's figures and discussion; they are the paper's own reported results, not invented.

outputs.description: Cementite Mn mass content vs soft-annealing temperature. The checker verifies the overall trend (Mn content increases as temperature decreases) and compares the value at 650°C to the paper's reference (~17 mass%) within a tolerance.

Equilibrium austenite Ms temperature vs intercritical annealing temperature. The checker checks that Ms decreases monotonically with temperature and compares each point to paper-derived gold within a tolerance.

Driving forces for paraequilibrium austenite formation from cementite and ferrite. The checker verifies that the driving force for γ_c^p is greater than for γ_α^p at every temperature and compares values to paper-derived gold within tolerance.

schema.description: A single floating-point number on its own line, representing Ms temperature in °C.

outputs.description: Ms temperature estimate for austenite that inherits 17% Mn and 0.5% C from cementite. The checker compares the value to the paper's estimate (-10°C) within a tolerance.

output_contract.notes: This task reproduces purely thermodynamic calculations supporting the claim of austenite stabilization via paraequilibrium cementite-to-austenite conversion. Experimental dilatometry, TEM, and EELS are not included. The checker uses paper-derived reference values and trend checks.
